rationale: The original review discusses this constituent in laboratory work without a fresh rosemary clinical depression comparison.
The survey records customary use. It gives no observed comparison for daytime sleepiness severity or Parkinson disease.
A contributor named the species as a bedtime option, with no firsthand lemongrass response or diagnostic information.

After six months, the original trial recorded fatigue in 2 (5%) beverage, 7 (18%) placebo capsule, and 10 (24%) EGCG capsule participants. Exposure to the beverage was open label. The prior-month occurrence counts do not measure Parkinson fatigue severity.
The review names green tea constituents. Its fatigue mention is clinical background for multiple sclerosis, with no brewed exposure fatigue contrast.
Within-tea fatigue decreased after a typing task. Beverage-by-time interaction was inconclusive. The linked October abstract is the same small acute crossover.
The public registry leaves beverage composition unspecified and gives no posted outcomes.
